text: Refactoring is the process of improving the structure of your code without changing what it actually does. Think of it like cleaning and reorganizing a messy room: the contents stay the same, but everything becomes easier to find and use. The main goal is to make the code more readable and maintainable. Common techniques include renaming unclear variables, breaking large functions into smaller ones, and removing duplicated logic. Over time, if we skip refactoring, we accumulate technical debt—the extra work needed later to fix poor design. By refactoring regularly, you save future time and reduce bugs, making your software healthier in the long run.
